drhp.business: CHL Limited owns and operates Hotel The Suryaa, a five-star landmark hotel in New Friends Colony, South Delhi, roughly a 20-minute drive from Connaught Place and 40 minutes from the domestic airport. Revenue comes from room sales plus food and beverage across a signature Pan-Asian restaurant, an all-day multi-cuisine outlet, a lounge bar and a wellness/fitness centre. The Company describes a portfolio of owned, leased and managed properties with a diversified brand architecture across geographies and segments, along with a stable stream of fee-based income.

risks.note: The auditors draw attention to note 26: the loan from EXIM Bank availed by CHL International, a subsidiary for which the Company is a guarantor, is a matter of litigation, with cases filed by EXIM Bank against the Company pending adjudication in the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India and the Debt Recovery Tribunal, Delhi. This is an off-balance-sheet exposure crystallised on the parent, not on the operating hotel.
risks.risk: Corporate guarantee on the subsidiary's EXIM Bank loan — the auditor's Emphasis of Matter

risks.note: EXIM Bank, the Principal Borrower and the Guarantors entered into a One Time Settlement for an amount of USD 34 million (EXIM Bank approval letter dated 23.11.2023), and the Economic Court of Dushanbe crystalized the liability against the borrowers/guarantors at USD 34 million by judgement dated 12.12.2023 in Case No. 52/2023. The OTS was still under implementation as on the balance sheet date, so the exposure is not extinguished and non-performance would revive the full claim.
risks.risk: One Time Settlement of USD 34 million still only 'under implementation'

risks.note: EXIM Bank has filed separate applications in pending Original Applications — Transfer Application No. 221 of 2022 (EXIM Bank vs Dr. Lalit Kumar Malhotra) and Transfer Application No. 224 of 2022 (EXIM Bank vs CHL Limited) — before Debt Recovery Tribunal-III against the personal and corporate guarantors, meaning the litigation runs on multiple fora simultaneously and ties promoter-family personal guarantees to the Company's.
risks.risk: Parallel personal and corporate guarantee proceedings before DRT-III

risks.note: The MD&A 'Risk and concerns' section says that based on the assessment carried out during the year, no material or significant risks have been identified that are likely to adversely affect the business, operations or financial performance. That assertion sits alongside an unresolved guarantee litigation flagged by the statutory auditors, so the disclosed risk framework understates the actual exposure and gives an investor little visibility into risk monitoring.
risks.risk: Management states no material risks were identified, despite the auditor's Emphasis of Matter

risks.note: The entire operating narrative rests on one property, Hotel The Suryaa in New Friends Colony, South Delhi. Revenue, occupancy and ARR all depend on one micro-market, one asset's condition and one city's demand cycle; any localised disruption, regulatory action or refurbishment shutdown has no offsetting property.

The MD&A states that while revenue remained broadly stable, profitability was impacted due to the payment of a long-pending Property Tax litigation liability, which was settled and paid during the year. A single legacy municipal-tax settlement was large enough to move reported profitability materially, showing that unresolved statutory disputes are a real earnings risk for a company of this size.
risks.risk: Litigated statutory liabilities can hit earnings in lumps

risks.note: The MD&A threats discussion flags the Middle East conflict, which has disrupted airspace, reduced travel flows to the region and affected destinations relying on the Middle East as a key global transit hub handling around 14% of all international passengers. For a Delhi hotel dependent on international and corporate arrivals, a hit to connectivity and traveller confidence feeds directly into occupancy and rate.

The cautionary statement enumerates the risk factors the Company itself names: changes in economic conditions, government policies, regulatory developments and industry trends, all beyond its control, with actual results potentially differing materially from stated expectations.
risks.risk: Forward-looking exposure to macro, policy and regulatory change
